rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.
Test temperature selectivity while keeping the gradient unchanged, targeting the nearly coeluting late cluster. Higher temperature should also create time headroom for a shallower gradient if needed.

Change only gradient duration to measure how the unresolved early pair and late cluster respond to slope. This modestly shallower gradient should keep the last peak near 10 minutes while revealing whether further slope adjustment is worthwhile.

Raise the starting organic fraction to trim the early elution window while making the gradient shallower at the same duration. This tests whether the critical pairs can gain resolution without pushing the last peak beyond 10 minutes or excessively compressing the first peaks.

Probe the low-temperature selectivity branch using the original gradient, since raising temperature improved the late cluster but worsened an early pair. This comparison will show whether cooling separates the critical groups in a more favorable order.

Test a substantially steeper gradient to check for useful elution-order changes in the critical clusters. The shallower-gradient branch is already approaching the time penalty, so this run explores a faster alternative rather than extending it blindly.

Explore a narrower, shallower gradient with a higher starting fraction to spread the late critical pair while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes. This also tests whether the early cluster separates again after its apparent selectivity crossover, balanced against possible loss of first-pair resolution.

Step the starting fraction upward to test the other side of the early-cluster crossover and further reduce gradient slope. Monitor the first three peaks closely for compression while seeking better resolution of the late critical pair.

Test temperature selectivity within the best gradient window, aiming to move the early near-coeluting pair away from its crossover. This isolates temperature effects while checking whether gains in that cluster outweigh any loss in late-pair resolution or time.

Return to the low starting fraction that preserved the early peaks, using an intermediate temperature to balance the early and late critical clusters. The slightly shallower slope than injection 2 should improve separation while keeping the last peak close to 10 minutes.

Test a shallower slope at the intermediate starting fraction, where the early cluster was less crowded than at 0.20 organic. This measures whether improved middle and late separations compensate for a possible small time penalty.

Explore a different selectivity branch with a higher starting fraction and cooler column, which may separate clusters after elution-order reversals. Cooling should partly counter early-peak compression, while the trimmed window leaves time headroom.

Test the cooler, steeper branch in the trimmed window, where temperature and slope may move the late cluster through its elution-order crossover. The shorter gradient should avoid the time penalty observed at 45 C.

Explore a gradient-to-hold alternative, placing the late critical cluster near the transition to the final hold to change its selectivity. The higher temperature and moderate final organic fraction should limit late retention, although this run may incur a time penalty.

Refine the best method with a slightly shallower slope, using its remaining time headroom to improve the late critical pair. The final fraction remains above the observed elution window, so all peaks should still elute during the gradient.

Combine modest cooling with a shallower gradient at the higher starting fraction to improve the early cluster and first-three-peak spacing. This tests whether those selectivity gains can outweigh the temperature-related loss in late-pair resolution while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes.

Refine the promising higher-starting-fraction branch with a shallower slope and a small temperature increase to improve the late critical pair. The lower endpoint also tests whether a short final hold can preserve separation without a substantial time penalty.

Fine-tune the best branch to a slope of 0.045 organic fraction per minute, using most of the remaining headroom below a 10-minute last peak. This should modestly improve the late critical pair without introducing the low-endpoint hold penalty seen in injection 17.

Test the unexamined starting fraction between the two promising low-organic methods, with a slope chosen to keep the last peak near 10 minutes. This checks whether the early cluster can improve without sacrificing too much first-pair or late-pair resolution.

Refine injection 16 by cooling one step to improve the early cluster and slightly steepening the gradient to offset the added retention. This targets a better balance of critical-pair resolutions with the last peak just below 10 minutes.

Test a five-degree temperature reduction on the intermediate-starting-fraction branch to improve the first pair and rebalance the early cluster. This checks whether those gains outweigh the expected loss in late-pair resolution and added retention.

Cool one more step to improve the first pair and balance the early cluster, while steepening the gradient to bring the last peak back toward 10 minutes. This targets the promising resolution term of injection 21 without its time penalty.

Retain the improved selectivity of injection 21 but increase the slope just enough to target a last peak near 10 minutes. This tests whether its strong resolution term can be preserved while removing the time penalty.

Test the next shallower practical slope around the best method to determine whether improved critical-pair resolution outweighs a small time penalty. This brackets the apparent optimum near a 10-minute last peak.

Fine-tune the strong low-starting-organic branch with a slope just steeper than injection 3, targeting a last peak immediately below 10 minutes. This should retain most of its critical-pair resolution while eliminating its time penalty.
